label: rem:mass-categorical-descent-argument
title: Argument for mass categorical descent (not a proof)
html:
Argument (not a proof). Over a field R for which H_n(R,q) is split semisimple (e.g. q not a root of unity in characteristic 0), the Wedderburn–Artin decomposition H_n(R,q)\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}M_{d_\lambda}(R) identifies Z(H_n(q)) with the block scalars. Over a general commutative ring this decomposition does not hold. In the split semisimple case the algebra has a centre–cocentre splitting, and the central part of an element x is \sum_\lambda\frac{\chi^\lambda(x)}{d_\lambda}e_\lambda (Centre–cocentre splitting, item 6).

The scalar sum \mathfrak m=\sum_i\ln|M_i| is a real number rather than an element of H_n(q), so the algebra-level centre–cocentre split cannot be applied directly to \mathfrak m; labelling terms that factor through a block's Casimir eigenvalue as "descended" is a definition rather than a theorem. Consequently, the Wedderburn–Artin splitting establishes nothing beyond the theorem cited and does not derive the liquid-drop term pairings in the conjecture statement.
